transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that review-type agents should run on a different model family from the implementer. The org-default review model was to be pinned to a different family, and the settings UI would warn when the two resolved to the same family. An amendment dated 2026-10-14 reversed this. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. A local bench on five merged PRs showed Argon catching more known must-fixes than Sonnet, which outweighed the self-preference risk. The amendment says cross-family review is 'no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice'. The cost is that Argon is about 3x slower and about 40% dearer. I read only the excerpts of the ADR and PR #1091 (the earlier model-family warning helpers), not the full documents.

judgements.reason: The answer matches the gold: ADR-039 set cross-family review as the rule, the 2026-10-14 amendment moved code-review and code-review-recheck to gemini-4-argon (same family) because it caught more, and cross-family is now only one input to the model choice.

The answer says cross-family review is no longer required, cites ADR-039 and its 2026-10-14 amendment moving code-review and code-review-recheck to gemini-4-argon in the implementer's family because it caught more, and notes cross-family is now only one input.
